{{Quote|I am more than Sith, now. Much more.|Sadic|<ref name="Showdown" />}}
'''Sadic''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]] during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. [[Reproduction/Legends|Born]] to [[Sadic's parents|low-class parents]], Sadic's [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitivity]] gained him admission to the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], and he orchestrated the [[Death/Legends|deaths]] of many rival [[Sith acolyte/Legends|acolytes]] at the Academy before he became the [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] and personal [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Umbriss]]. After Umbriss was killed by his superior [[Darth Angral]], Sadic became Angral's apprentice, and he achieved the rank of Sith Lord alongside his fellows [[Praven]] and [[Nefarid]]. When Angral's son, [[Tarnis (Sith Lord)|Tarnis]], was [[Duel in the Jedi Temple ruins|killed]] by a [[Hero of Tython|Jedi Knight]] in [[3643 BBY]], Sadic was sent to the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] to take control of the Republic's [[Power Guard Enhancement System|Power Guard]] supersoldier project as part of Angral's [[Desolator crisis|war of vengeance]] against the Republic. Willingly undergoing the Power Guard process himself in order to gain further power, Sadic planned to fashion an [[Army/Legends|army]] of Power Guards from the throngs of [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]] who made Nar Shaddaa their home, but he was killed before his plans could come to fruition by the same [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] who had killed Tarnis.

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|What's this, Tarnis? A loose end? For shame.|Sadic|<ref name="Race to the Ruins" />}}
A [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]],<ref name="Model" /> the man later known as Sadic was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] to [[Sadic's parents|lower-class parents]] within the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], and because of his family's status, he began his life only one step above a [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] in Imperial society. However, Sadic soon demonstrated [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitivity]]<ref name="Sadic" /> sometime after the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[3681 BBY]],<ref name="Timeline 6">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 6: Onslaught of the Sith Empire|int=Timeline 6: Onslaught of the Sith Empire}} states that [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] was [[Battle of Korriban|reclaimed]] in [[3681 BBY]], meaning Sadic had to be sent there sometime afterward.</ref> which caused him to be sent off to the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. Sadic was the only [[Sith acolyte/Legends|acolyte]] in his entire group to survive the trials on Korriban, as he [[Death/Legends|murdered]] many of his fellow [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentices]] and other Academy residents during his [[Time/Legends|time]] there. He was never suspected of the crimes, however, and the murders only stopped when Sadic finally left the planet to become the apprentice of the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Umbriss]]. Sadic served as Umbriss's personal [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] for several [[Standard year/Legends|years]] until Umbriss incurred the wrath of the more powerful [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Darth Angral]] and was killed for his transgressions. Angral acquired Sadic along with [[Umbriss's estate|Umbriss' estate]] and the rest of his wealth, and although Sadic pledged eternal loyalty to Angral, the elder Sith recognized that Sadic would likely kill him if given the chance and kept him on a tight leash.<ref name="Sadic" /> Under Angral's tutelage, Sadic achieved the rank of Sith [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] during the time of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

[[File:Sadic_and_Nefarid.png|thumb|right|200px|Nefarid and Sadic speak with Tarnis.]]
In [[3643 BBY]],<ref name="Time" /> Sadic entered into a holoconference with Angral and Angral's son, [[Tarnis (Sith Lord)|Tarnis]], along with the Sith Lord's other apprentices, [[Praven]] and [[Nefarid]]. Angral and his apprentices were using a [[Imperial Listening Post|secret Imperial facility]] on the planet [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] to contact Tarnis, while Tarnis was on the Republic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where he had abandoned his undercover assignment of posing as a Republic [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] in order to steal the [[Planet Prison]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] and use it against Coruscant. Tarnis was setting up the weapon in the depths of the ruined [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]], and he was informing his father and Angral's apprentices of the success of his mission when a [[Hero of Tython|young Jedi Knight]] arrived with the [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Kira Carsen]]. Amused to see how Tarnis had failed to eliminate his [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] pursuers, Sadic mocked Tarnis for his failure to wrap up loose ends, and he watched along with Angral and the others as Tarnis engaged the two Jedi in a [[Duel in the Jedi Temple ruins|duel]]. However, Tarnis was struck down by the Knight in the fighting, and a furious Angral [[Desolator crisis|declared war]] on the Republic as a result.<ref name="Race to the Ruins" />

===The Power Guard Project===
{{Quote|Mark One Power Guards. Not as destructive as the later models I possess, but quick to assemble and quite malleable. It took nothing to wipe their useless minds and program them to serve me.''"<br />"''You twisted&hellip; what have you done to these people?''"<br />"''Perfected them. What good is a weapon you can't control?|Sadic and the Knight|<ref name="The Search for Agent Galen" />}}
[[File:Sadic_holo.png|thumb|left|150px|Sadic on Nar Shaddaa, before the Power Guard process]]
Using information on the Republic's weapons projects that he had received from Tarnis before his death, Angral dispatched his apprentices to take control of the projects as part of his crusade for revenge. Sadic was tasked with seizing the [[Power Guard Enhancement System]], a project focused on the creation of supersoldiers through [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetics]] and [[Adrenal/Legends|adrenals]], on the neutral [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. With a complement of [[Imperial soldier]]s, Sadic located the [[Power Guard Cybernetics Lab]] in Nar Shaddaa's [[Red Light Sector (Nar Shaddaa)|Red Light Sector]], and his forces captured the lab along with the [[Power Guard recruitment center]] in the [[Nikto Sector]]. While the Imperials began to send captive recruits to the lab for "testing," Sadic's [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] captured [[Agent/Legends|Agent]] [[Galen (SIS)|Galen]] of the [[Republic Strategic Information Service]], the Republic's intelligence agency, in an attempt to infiltrate the center. Intrigued, Sadic ordered the agent to be brought to the lab,<ref name="The Search for Agent Galen">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|The Search for Agent Galen|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref> where the Sith performed the Power Guard process on Galen and replaced two-thirds of the man's body with cybernetics.<ref name="Showdown" />

Upon failing to receive any communications from his men at the recruitment center,<ref name="Red Light">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Red Light, Black Heart|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref> Sadic retreated to another [[Sadic's laboratory|facility]] in the Imperial [[Prison/Legends|prison]] district of [[Shadow Town]], where he began to put in motion his plans to construct an [[Army/Legends|army]] of Power Guards from the [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]] present on Nar Shaddaa.<ref name="Showdown" /> He left behind [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Graul (Human)|Graul]] and a small group of soldiers to defend the main project [[Laboratory/Legends|lab]], promising the [[Officer/Legends|officer]] that he could personally execute the person responsible for the deaths of the men at the recruitment center, and his suspicions about that individual's identity were confirmed when the Knight who had killed Tarnis arrived at the project lab. Speaking to the Knight and the Jedi's companion via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]], Sadic explained that he had left several [[Mark I Power Guard]]s behind to aid Graul, and the Sith's callous disregard for the lives of those whom he had converted appalled the Knight before Sadic ended the transmission.<ref name="Red Light" /> Sadic then dispatched a [[Squad/Legends|squad]] of [[Mark II Power Guard]]s to the recently uncovered [[SIS safe house|SIS base]] at the [[Promenade]] shopping complex.<ref name="Striking Back">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Striking Back|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref>

{{GameLS|Star Wars: The Old Republic}}
[[File:Sadic_Power_Guard.png|thumb|right|170px|Sadic as a Power Guard]]
Under Sadic's orders, Agent Galen confronted the Knight in an [[Imperial weapons factory]] in the [[Lower Industrial Sector]], and Sadic took pleasure in [[Torture/Legends|torturing]] Galen through his implants in order to force the agent to obey. Galen proceeded to attack the Jedi after Sadic ended his holotransmission to the agent. Though Galen was able to break free of Sadic's commands with the help of the Jedi, Sadic then proceeded to willingly undergo the Power Guard process himself to increase his power. The Knight then assaulted Sadic's base in Shadow Town, defeating several [[Mark III Power Guard]]s and the Imperial defenders before finding Sadic in the facility's main room. Flanked by two Power Guards, the newly-upgraded Sith marveled at the added power granted to him by the Power Guard technology, as he was able to calculate seventeen different ways to kill the Jedi within the short time that he was speaking with his opponent.<ref name="Showdown" />

While Sadic was contemplating whether to add the Knight to his army of Power Guards, Galen charged in to support the Jedi, and an amused Sadic used voice commands to raise the level of control over the converted agent. However, Galen was able to push through the pain and join the Knight to battle Sadic, and the Sith drew his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] to press the offensive. Sadic's increased strength and the support of his Power Guards were not enough to overcome the Knight, the Jedi's companion, and Galen, and the battle ended with Sadic's death. Not long afterward, Sadic's body was destroyed when the Republic [[Commando/Legends|commando]] unit [[Blackstar Squad]] demolished the lab with explosives at the Knight's orders.<ref name="Showdown" /> Upon learning of Sadic's death, Nefarid sent a message to the Knight congratulating the Jedi on defeating Sadic, and he thanked the Knight for the elimination of one of his rivals for Angral's favor.<ref name="A Job">{{TORcite|type=message|A Job Well Done|Lord Nefarid}}</ref>
{{Endgame}}

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|No price is too high to become war incarnate.|Sadic|<ref name="Showdown" />}}
[[File:Sadic_mask.png|thumb|left|150px|Sadic's mask]]
A Human male with light skin, blue [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and black [[Hair/Legends|hair]],<ref name="Model" /> Sadic was of average height and small build before he underwent the Power Guard process.<ref name="Race to the Ruins" /> However, after the Power Guard process, Sadic was significantly taller and more physically imposing. Over two-thirds of Sadic's biological mass was replaced by cybernetics during the process, and Sadic viewed the exchange of his humanity for an increase in power to be an excellent trade.<ref name="Showdown" /> Sadic was very ambitious and determined even as a young acolyte, and he was willing to murder his fellow acolytes in order to remove rivals.<ref name="Sadic" /> Like many of the Empire's inhabitants, Sadic viewed [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] as little better than animals, and he was perfectly at ease with conducting the Power Guard process on unwilling subjects.<ref name="Red Light" /> The Sith took pleasure in inflicting pain on others and found Galen's resistance to his mental control as an amusing obstacle that could be overcome by inflicting more pain.<ref name="Showdown" />

==Equipment==
Sadic wore a [[Color/Legends|silver]]-and-gray mask with red [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and metallic mandible-like attachments over his mouth, and he typically wore dark, [[hood]]ed [[Robe/Legends|robes]] with a [[Belt/Legends|belt]], on which he hooked his red-bladed lightsaber.<ref name="Race to the Ruins" /> After his body was enhanced by the Power Guard process, he donned additional shoulder [[Armor/Legends|armor]] to complement his increased size.<ref name="Showdown" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|Remarkable technology. So versatile. I just calculated seventeen different ways to end your life.|Sadic|<ref name="Showdown" />}}
Sadic was strong in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and proficient in the use of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]], and he wielded a red-bladed lightsaber in combat. After undergoing the Power Guard conversion process, Sadic's reflexes and physical strength were greatly increased, and his mind was able to process a combat situation and quickly assess his opponents' strengths and weaknesses. The enhancements also allowed Sadic to run through scenarios and calculate probabilities in order to determine the most efficient and effective way of defeating opponents.<ref name="Showdown" />

==Behind the scenes==
Lord Sadic first appeared as a recurring character in the storyline for the Jedi Knight class in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', a [[Star Wars video games|video game]] released by [[BioWare]] and [[LucasArts]] in [[2011]]. Sadic appears in hologram form in the mission "Race to the Ruins," and he serves as the primary antagonist on Nar Shaddaa for the Jedi Knight.<ref name="Showdown" /> The "Fate of the Galaxy" trailer, released at PAX East 2011, showed footage of Angral watching a space battle as Sadic and Nefarid approach him, though that scene, like several others featured in the trailer, never made it into the game.<ref name="Fate">{{TORweb|url=info/news/news-article/20110311|text=PAX East Trailer: Fate of the Galaxy}}</ref> The fight with Sadic can change depending on whether or not the player helps Agent Galen break free of Sadic's control. If players refuse to kill Galen, they receive fifty [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light-side]] alignment points, and Galen will run off in anger. The player will later find Galen in Sadic's base, where he is heavily injured after having defeated most of the Power Guard defenders. If players do kill him, they receive dark-side alignment points and fight Sadic alone. However, if players convince him to fight Sadic, they receive 100 alignment points, and Galen will aid the player in the final battle with Sadic.<ref name="Showdown" />

The player also has three choices for what to do with the Power Guard project after Sadic's death: destroy the project and the lab for light-side points, take it for the Republic and receive dark-side alignment points, or sabotage the project for dark-side points.<ref name="Showdown" /> This article assumes that the player chooses only the moral light-side options that give the maximum amount of alignment points as a Republic Jedi Knight character<ref name="Light Side">This article assumes that the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] classes in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' choose the options that provide the most [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light-side]] alignment points.</ref> and therefore assumes that Galen was convinced to aid the Knight and that the player destroyed the project.<ref name="Showdown" /> The [[2012]] reference guide ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]'' featured a mention of Sadic, Nefarid, and Praven in the entry for [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Angral.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />
